default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1438.title: VWAP stretch fade in ATR units
E-1438.hypothesis: A close several average bar-ranges away from session VWAP is an over-extension by impatient aggressors; liquidity providers and VWAP-benchmarked algos pull price back, so fade the first bar of the stretch.

E-1439.title: Short/long ATR expansion follow
E-1439.hypothesis: When the 10-minute average range jumps relative to the 60-minute one, a new information flow has arrived and the first expansion bar's direction tends to persist while slower participants catch up.

E-1440.title: Dollar-leads, index-lags inverse
E-1440.hypothesis: WIN and WDO are normally inversely related; when the dollar makes an unusual move and the index has not yet reacted, index arbitrageurs/hedgers move WIN the opposite way a few minutes later.

E-1441.title: Day-open reclaim after a stay
E-1441.hypothesis: After price spends a while on one side of the session open, a close back through it shows the earlier side's positions are under water; follow the cross.

E-1442.title: Three expanding strong bars follow
E-1442.hypothesis: Three same-direction bodies with widening ranges show escalating urgency of one side; follow the third.

E-1443.title: Clock-hour open magnet fade
E-1443.hypothesis: Hourly opens are anchors for desks that mark intraday P&L by the hour; a large drift away from the current hour's open tends to partly revert.

E-1444.title: Up-bar share persistence
E-1444.hypothesis: When nearly all recent bars close in one colour, a persistent one-sided order flow (e.g. a large parent order sliced over time) is being worked; follow its onset.

E-1445.title: Volume dry-up then expansion follow
E-1445.hypothesis: After several low-volume bars, a sudden volume burst marks the end of balance; the burst bar's colour gives the direction of the new initiative.

E-1446.title: Index and dollar moving together fade
E-1446.hypothesis: WIN and WDO usually move in opposite directions; when both make a large move the same way it is usually a transient dislocation (one leg is a flow-driven error) and WIN reverts.

E-1447.title: Late-session open-stretch fade
E-1447.hypothesis: Late in the session, day-traders who held a large open-to-now move square up before the close, so an unusually stretched price (vs the same-minute typical) reverts toward the open.
